title: Join weekly stocks to daily prices with merge_asof — backward, on availability

explain.prompt: In 4–6 sentences: why must the join be done on `available_at` with `direction='backward'`, and what would `week_ending` as the key do? Why is a backward join on the right key still only a necessary condition for point-in-time correctness? What do `age_days` and the tolerance protect you from?
rubric: Backward on available_at = for each decision, the last report already published before the 14:30 settlement — never a later one.

Keyed on week_ending, the stock level of a week would be attached to prices from the Friday it describes, 5–6 days before its release: on about 630 of 1,042 days the join uses a report not yet published.

Backward + availability key + right vintage = point-in-time. A backward join only guarantees right key ≤ left key: if the key is the observation date, or the value is a later revision, it still leaks.
age_days (decision − week_ending, here 5 to 12 days) shows how stale the matched information is; a growing age signals an interrupted series.
The tolerance (10 days) prevents matching a value that is too old (e.g. after a missed release) — better NaN than a silently stale number; the first two days of 2016 have no report yet and stay NaN.
Different frequencies (weekly vs daily) are aligned without interpolation: the weekly value is carried until the next release, as a trader would.
